discoveryScope: auto (the surface's default: the workspace's own VCS inventory; vendored and ignored trees excluded)

identityCollisions.detail: more than one declaration reduces to this identity; the surface's id is a slug and carries no line, so these declarations are not separately addressable through it. Check the sites before calling it a source-side duplication: discovery is a static scan and is blind to `when` selection, so declarations in mutually exclusive branches collide here while at most one of them exists in any given build. That is a limitation of the identity (it has no configuration dimension), not necessarily a defect in the source

surface.provenance: built from metacraft-labs/codetracer e1b5280a2755f4c5016679610d208e5b94d1d5ec — the codetracer-src revision pinned in reprobuild flake.lock — with the ctTestTools recipe: nim c --threads:on --mm:orc --out:build/bin/ct-test src/ct_test/ct_test.nim

title: Reprobuild case addressability through the canonical `ct test` surface

unaddressableSources.detail: imports the vendored ct_test_unittest_parallel shim instead of std/unittest. Note what does NOT happen: the provider's `frameworkForImport` matches the literal names `unittest`, `unittest2` and `unittest_parallel`, and `ct_test_unittest_parallel` is none of them — so no framework is detected, no `detected but not implemented` warning is emitted (the workspace response carries zero of those), and the file falls through the same generic path as any non-test source, reported as `no Nim unittest imports detected in file`. Implementing unittest_parallel support upstream would therefore NOT recover these rows; retiring the shim would

imports std/unittest inside a bracketed clause spanning more than one line; the provider's framework scan is line-oriented and never sees the continuation, so the file is never scanned for declarations.
